Role: Staff Engineer (Integrations / Supply, air travel)
Company: Voyagu
Location: Fully remote, Europe preferred. European time zone; about two hours of difference is fine. About eight hours online, and some overlap with US time zones helps because many users are there.
Job Type: Full-time. Contract model is flexible: contractor, payroll provider or direct employment.
About Voyagu
Voyagu builds one platform that runs several travel businesses. Today the focus is air travel. The platform covers client management (CRM), ERP modules for finance and accounting, travel operations, and integrations with travel supply systems.
The model is offline travel: agencies that sell through people. Voyagu does not sell the software and does not plan to, but agencies work with it in different models. It is a bootstrap scaleup, so teams are lean and money is counted.
Development leans heavily on AI. Teams of AI agents run big features under a business operator and a technical operator. Sometimes this turns two half-years of work into two weeks. It does not always work. When code is cheap, product vision and architecture become the bottleneck, and that is where you come in.
This role owns the integrations and supply direction. Air travel alone is deep: every airline has its own distribution channels and APIs. You would lead one of five platform development streams and report to the CTO. There is no product manager in between, and you work directly with the founder and other business stakeholders. The team has no one with your profile today, so you would be the first.
What you are expected to do
Technical ownership
• 
Lead the integrations and supply direction as its technical owner.
• 
Build integrations with GDS systems. Voyagu works with one today and needs more.
• 
Connect airline direct APIs and non-GDS protocols across multiple sources.
• 
Handle servicing after sale: changes, cancellations, refunds, and group bookings split into parts.
• 
Work with live, real-time availability. Seat availability does not depend on price.
• 
Prevent costly errors. One missed booking can mean tens of thousands of dollars. Design for reliability, for example with idempotency, so nothing is paid or bought twice.
• 
Keep the solution sized to Voyagu’s scale and avoid over-design. This is not internet-scale work.
• 
Keep the system stable. Speed and error rate are the measures.
Vision and delivery
• 
Shape the technical vision with stakeholders and defend it. They will challenge it.
• 
Expect no ready-made tasks. Business stakeholders give you a direction, not a finished task.
• 
Turn the agreed platform capabilities into features and give estimates. Several dozen capabilities are written down, such as search and booking.
• 
Success means Voyagu accepts your estimates and you deliver them, or come close. Part of the plan will be agreed together with you.
AI-driven development
• 
Build and direct teams of AI coding agents instead of writing code by hand.
• 
Explain and defend how to use AI effectively.
• 
Bring AI practices that are as good as Voyagu’s, or better.
Team
• 
Lead the two people already working in this direction, once you have onboarded.
• 
Hire as little as possible. Hiring is a last resort. Long term the direction may grow to one to three people.
What you need to succeed
• 
You have worked in the travel domain, especially on integrations with supply systems. About two or more years is likely enough.
• 
You understand booking versus ticket, and the statuses and states of each.
• 
You have owned a large piece of a product, not a small slice.
• 
You work at staff or senior level, as architect and technical lead.
• 
You understand what Voyagu does and why, and you talk well with stakeholders.
• 
You use AI well beyond the beginner level and have a clear view on how to use it effectively.
• 
You believe small teams work. You do not think in big organisations.
• 
You work in a European time zone; ideally you are based in Europe.
• 
You speak Russian: engineering works mostly in Russian. Business teams speak English, and English B2 is enough.
• 
Nice to have: you have seen both corporate and lean startup worlds, or a bootstrap scaleup. You may be an ex-founder or a small-company CTO who stayed hands-on.
• 
Nice to have: you have run teams of agents, not only asked an agent to write a feature.
• 
Nice to have: vendor-side experience building for end users. Python is the current main stack, but language skill is not important.
• 
Not required: high-load experience, writing agent skills, or deep C#/legacy aviation knowledge.
What you get
• 
You own a whole direction, with responsibility handed over fully.
• 
You are the technical lead for integrations and supply, with no product-manager layer in between.
• 
You work with AI agent teams. Voyagu will invest heavily in tokens and compute where it pays off.
• 
You can bring AI practices better than Voyagu’s own, and the team will share theirs.
• 
A large, technically hard platform: real-time inventory, many sources, money at stake.
• 
A lean environment with few meetings and flexible hours.
• 
Fully remote in Europe, with flexible contract models.
• 
Equity is not standard, but it is negotiable for an exceptional candidate.
How to apply
Apply through hirehire, the agency running this search for Voyagu. The process has three stages: an engineering interview with the CTO, a travel-domain interview with the founder, and a practical case with a defence.

The Team + The Role

Pendo’s Growth Marketing team owns the engine that creates predictable, efficient demand across paid, organic, lifecycle, and product-led channels. The team connects marketing strategy, analytics, experimentation, and cross-functional execution to generate qualified pipeline and improve the buyer and user journey.

As VP, Growth Marketing, you will lead Pendo’s full growth engine from top-of-funnel awareness through qualified pipeline creation. You will own demand generation, website performance, marketing analytics, experimentation, lifecycle programs, and product-led growth motions while partnering closely with Sales, Product, the CMO, the CRO, and the executive team.

Remote in the United States

What this looks like day-to-day

• Demand generation and pipeline: Own demand generation strategy and execution across paid search, paid social, SEO/GEO, content-driven acquisition, and multi-channel campaigns. Build programs that generate qualified pipeline and improve the efficiency and predictability of growth.

• Cross-functional partnership: Partner closely with Sales on pipeline handoff and conversion, with Product on growth features and activation, and with the CMO and CRO on GTM priorities and investment allocation. Bring a clear growth point of view to executive and operator-level decisions.

• Marketing website performance: Own the marketing website as a core growth asset, including performance, conversion rate optimization, experimentation, lead routing, and continuous improvement of the buyer journey and demo experience. Partner with the CMO, VP of Product Marketing, and design team on UX/UI elements and product page content.

• Paid creative strategy: Bring a strong point of view on paid creative and partner with the broader marketing team on evergreen paid assets and integrated campaign assets. Ensure the team tracks creative performance and understands why each asset wins or loses.

• Marketing analytics and attribution: Build and maintain clear attribution models, dashboards, and reporting that give leadership accurate visibility into what drives pipeline and revenue. Use measurement infrastructure to guide prioritization, investment decisions, and budget efficiency.

• Experimentation system: Establish a rigorous testing culture across acquisition, the website, onboarding, and lifecycle. Identify what works, scale successful tests, and create a system for continuous improvement.

• Team leadership: Build, lead, and develop a high-performing growth organization across demand generation, performance marketing, SEO/GEO, website, analytics, and product/lifecycle growth. Create a team culture defined by ownership, pace, measurement, and cross-functional alignment.

• Product-led and lifecycle growth: Drive activation, onboarding, time-to-value, retention, and expansion programs that increase product adoption and net revenue retention. Connect product-led and lifecycle motions to broader pipeline, revenue, and customer growth outcomes.

Who You Are

Beyond the qualifications, we hire through a specific lens. These aren't buzzwords; they're the things we'll actually look for in how you talk about your work.

You're a builder, not a maintainer.

You're most energized when there isn't a clear path yet, and you get to define it. You don't wait for direction; you identify gaps, shape solutions, and drive them forward. At Pendo, great VPs of Growth Marketing don't just follow instructions; they operate as strategic advisors, influencing decisions, guiding stakeholders, and elevating how we work.

You're AI-curious - genuinely.

You're not using AI tools occasionally. You're rewiring how you work around them. You're faster, sharper, and more prolific because of it, and you bring that energy to everything — how you approach your work, how you prep, how you communicate, how you think. We want someone who sees AI as a multiplier, not a shortcut.

Must-haves

• 12+ years of experience in growth, demand generation, or revenue marketing within B2B SaaS, including significant leadership across performance channels and product-led or lifecycle motions.

• Proven track record owning demand generation across paid search, paid social, SEO, pipeline generation, and other growth channels, with measurable pipeline and revenue outcomes at scale.

• Direct experience managing marketing analytics, attribution, and website performance or conversion optimization.

• Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to build measurement infrastructure and use data to guide prioritization and investment decisions.

• Demonstrated ability to lead and scale cross-functional teams while influencing across Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to set clear priorities for executives and operators.

Nice-to-haves

• Experience in product analytics, digital adoption, or developer/product tools companies.

• Background scaling growth in hybrid self-serve and enterprise environments.

• Experience with SFDC, Omni, Clari, and/or other AI-driven revenue analytics tools.

About Pendo

Pendo was founded in 2013 by former product managers, who combined their heads and hearts to build something they wanted but never had as product managers: a simple way to understand and attack what truly drives product success. Our mission is to improve society's experience with software. Come join one of the fastest-growing startups, supported by best-in-class institutions like Battery Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Spark Capital and Meritech.
